method: Manual in-session triage (no subagents — monthly spend limit hit mid-run). Direct code re-verification: F-001, F-002, F-003, F-004, F-010, plus tree-wide grep confirming zero code-signature primitives. Remaining findings triaged by analysis of the scanner's cited code locations and its (well-calibrated) self-assessment, not re-opened line-by-line.
environment: Local single-user macOS app, unsandboxed, no remote listener. Same-uid local process IS in scope per THREAT_MODEL.md (e.g. a compromised dependency in a project the user runs an agent in), but impact is bounded by 'attacker already runs as the user'. The only true cross-privilege boundaries are cross-uid (multi-user host) and the update/supply-chain channel.

confirmed.title: Same-uid code-execution persistence via unprotected ~/.zackeyes launcher chain (no signature check, default perms)
confirmed.root_cause: ~/.zackeyes, its bin/ dir, the exec'd launcher script, and the .app-path marker are all created with default (umask) perms; the launcher resolves its exec target from the same-uid-writable marker (F-010) or an mdfind result (F-012) or a directly-overwritable script body (F-011), gating only on [-x] with zero code-signature verification. HookHealth (F-014) reports 'healthy' on path-equality alone, masking poisoning.
confirmed.severity_rationale: Stays HIGH: converts a one-shot same-uid write into PERSISTENT, agent-triggered code execution that re-fires on every hook — a persistence/foothold escalation within the in-scope same-uid threat (documented T3/EP8, marked unmitigated). Cheapest high-value fix in the set.
confirmed.fix: Create ~/.zackeyes + bin 0700, write launcher 0700 and marker 0600; refuse to read/exec if marker/dir is writable by anyone but owner; verify the resolved bundle's Designated Requirement (codesign -R) before exec; bake the absolute install path in at deploy time and treat the marker as a non-authoritative hint; drop the bare mdfind exec.

confirmed.title: Software update opened with no in-app signature/checksum verification and a server-controlled download host
confirmed.root_cause: browser_download_url is taken verbatim from the release JSON (no host/scheme allowlist), default URLSession follows cross-origin redirects silently (F-022), the DMG is written to a predictable tmp path (F-018/F-019) and handed to NSWorkspace.open with no signature or checksum compare (grep: zero sha256 refs). The published SHA-256 is website display copy the app never checks.
confirmed.verified: grep confirmed zero signature/checksum primitives; F-013 code path traced from scanner citations (not re-opened line-by-line)
confirmed.severity_rationale: Impact is critical (RCE on every client) but GATED on the threat model's T2 precondition — the attacker must first compromise the release repo or publish token. As a standalone code gap it is the defense that should exist beneath T2; HIGH priority to fix, but it does not grant compromise on its own.
confirmed.fix: Verify the DMG's Developer-ID signature + notarization (or a fetched checksum) before open; reconstruct the asset URL from owner/repo/tag/name instead of trusting browser_download_url; reject non-allowlisted redirect hosts; write to a fresh 0700 per-download dir.

confirmed.title: Cross-uid socket squat: bridge does not authenticate the server peer on world-writable /tmp
confirmed.root_cause: The server authenticates clients via getpeereid, but the bridge (client) does NOT authenticate the server. /tmp is world-writable+sticky, so another uid can pre-bind /tmp/zackeyes.sock before the app starts (the app's unlink fails EPERM on a foreign-owned sticky file); the victim's bridge then connects to the squatter, leaking prompt/cwd/transcript_path and obeying a forged allow decision. No wall-clock timeout (F-021) also lets the squatter hang every PermissionRequest.
confirmed.verified: by analysis of scanner citations — NOT re-opened. RECOMMEND fresh-eyes re-verify (cross-uid claim, the only one that crosses the user boundary).
confirmed.severity_rationale: The one finding that crosses a real privilege boundary (different local user), so notable — but the pre-start race + shared-/tmp + multi-user-host preconditions are uncommon for a personal Mac app (real for CI runners / lab / shared boxes).
confirmed.fix: Move the socket to a per-user 0700 dir an attacker cannot pre-create; on the client side getpeereid-verify the server and reject peerEUID != geteuid(); validate the reply shape; add a finite wall-clock ceiling that fails open to CC's native prompt.

confirmed.title: OSC-2 terminal-escape injection via raw cwd basename (both title writers)
confirmed.root_cause: sanitizePrompt strips C0/DEL but is applied only to the prompt portion; the cwd basename is interpolated raw into the OSC-2 title in BOTH writers (bridge-side F-004, app-side F-005) and written to another process's tty. cwd is attacker-influenceable (hook JSON / scanned transcript metadata / malicious repo dir name). F-023 (missing C1/ST stripping) folds in as a sanitizer-completeness note.
confirmed.verified: F-004 directly (code read); F-005 by analysis (same shape, independent writer)
confirmed.severity_rationale: Real cross-content-boundary injection (malicious repo -> victim's terminal), but bounded: requires a directory name literally containing ESC/BEL bytes, and modern target terminals (Ghostty, UTF-8) restrict the dangerous sequences. Could be HIGH on permissive terminals (OSC 52 clipboard write etc.).
confirmed.fix: Sanitize the whole composed title once inside oscEscape/writeIfPossible (so no field can bypass it), strip C1 (0x80-0x9F) too, and collapse the two duplicate OSC builders into one shared sanitized helper.

confirmed.title: Integer-overflow trap -> persistent crash-loop via crafted token-count fields
confirmed.root_cause: Untrusted usage token fields parsed as? Int and summed with trapping +/+= (no clamping). A single transcript line with input_tokens=9223372036854775807 traps computeSnapshot, which re-runs every 30s while the line stays in the 7-day window -> app crashes on every relaunch.
confirmed.severity_rationale: Clean deterministic availability crash-loop that disables the permission/usage UI; reachable via malicious-repo transcript content (not just same-uid). Not memory corruption.
confirmed.fix: Reject negative/absurd magnitudes at parse time and use overflow-safe accumulation (clamping/&+ with a cap) in the folds.

confirmed.title: Uncapped file reads bypass the aba2176 256MB cap (recurring-path memory DoS)
confirmed.root_cause: The 256MB+symlink gate from aba2176 was applied only to the Claude computeSnapshot path. Sibling whole-file readers remain uncapped: codex daily-token scan (F-001, every 30s), TaskExtractor (F-002, every Task* PostToolUse), spool replay (F-017, startup), pricing/usage caches (F-020, startup). A planted/grown multi-GB file is re-read whole.
confirmed.verified: F-001, F-002 directly; F-017/F-020 by analysis
confirmed.severity_rationale: Availability only; same-uid or malicious-repo can plant/grow the file. F-001/F-002 are the strong instances (hot recurring paths); F-017/F-020 are startup-only and weaker.
confirmed.fix: Route every untrusted read through the existing shouldScanTranscript helper (stat -> skip symlinks + over-cap), and bounded-tail-read where only recent content is needed.

confirmed.title: Pending-spool replay has no event-type allowlist -> session-state / permission-badge spoofing
confirmed.root_cause: The write side restricts spooling to replayableEvents; the read side replays ANY decodable .json through the same authenticated handler. A planted file injects fake sessions, forces fabricated error banners, or stamps permissionRisk=.yolo. (Correctly NOT auto-grantable: replayed PermissionRequest early-returns on responder==nil.)
confirmed.verified: by analysis of scanner citations — NOT re-opened
confirmed.severity_rationale: Security-surface UI spoofing that could mislead a user into approving; same-uid, no direct tool grant.
confirmed.fix: Enforce the same replayableEvents allowlist on the read side; never let a replayed event mutate permissionRisk; store the spool in a 0700 dir.

confirmed.title: Pending-spool writes raw prompts/cwd/transcript-paths world-readable (0644) in a 0755 dir
confirmed.root_cause: Spool dir created with no attributes (umask -> 0755) and files written .atomic (umask -> 0644). Raw hook JSON (prompts, cwd, transcript paths) is exposed to other local users, while the socket node is deliberately locked 0600 — an inconsistent boundary.
confirmed.verified: by analysis of scanner citations (scanner reported verifying home=0755, umask 022 on this machine) — NOT independently re-checked. RECOMMEND re-verify the cross-uid perms claim.
confirmed.severity_rationale: Cross-uid info disclosure on a multi-user host; on a single-user Mac the practical exposure is low, but the perms gap is real and contradicts the deliberate 0600 socket lock. Pairs with T-5 as the cross-uid angle.
confirmed.fix: Create the spool dir 0700 and write files 0600; consider not persisting raw prompt/transcript content at all.

confirmed.title: Notification title unsanitized + body sanitizer strips no control/bidi chars (UI spoofing)
confirmed.root_cause: Notification title is raw-interpolated (cwd basename) and the body sanitizer (a weaker namesake of the OSC one) strips no C0/C1/bidi chars. Notification Center renders plain text (no escape execution), so impact is UI spoofing (RTL-override/zero-width to misrepresent which project/agent fired), raising mis-taps.
confirmed.verified: by analysis of scanner citations — NOT re-opened
confirmed.severity_rationale: No code execution; UI-spoofing only. Same sanitization-centralization theme as T-3.
confirmed.fix: Strip C0/C1/DEL + Unicode bidi/format controls in both title and body; centralize control-char stripping in one shared helper for every untrusted-text sink; rename one sanitizePrompt to remove the false equivalence.

confirmed.title: Unbounded pendingBuffer in kqueue tailer on a newline-free rollout line
confirmed.root_cause: The incremental parser carries the trailing partial line in an uncapped pendingBuffer (pending + chunk on each .write); a same-uid writer appending a huge newline-free line grows it to GB with O(n^2) recopy. F-026 (offset not reset on in-place truncation) folds in as a related robustness defect.
confirmed.verified: by analysis of scanner citations — NOT re-opened
confirmed.severity_rationale: Same-uid availability DoS / UI staleness; head reads are already bounded.
confirmed.fix: Cap pendingBuffer (drop/reset past a few-MB line ceiling); detect shrinkage (endSize < offset) and reset offset + clear buffer on truncation.

confirmed.title: Untrusted transcript_path passed to lsof without a -- end-of-options guard
confirmed.root_cause: lsof -t <file> with file from the untrusted transcript_path and no -- guard; a leading-dash value is parsed as an lsof option. argv-array invocation (no shell), and lsof exposes no write/exec flags, so impact is option-confusion (wrong/failed PID resolution), not RCE.
confirmed.verified: by analysis of scanner citations — NOT re-opened
confirmed.fix: Insert -- before the filename and reject transcript_path values not beginning with /.

downgraded_or_rejected.title: OSC sanitizer doesn't strip C1/ST
downgraded_or_rejected.reason: The scanner's own analysis is correct: the title is UTF-8 encoded at the write boundary, so U+009C is emitted as 0xC2 0x9C and never reaches a UTF-8 terminal as an 8-bit C1 ST. Valid defense-in-depth sanitizer-completeness suggestion only. Folded into T-3 as a hardening note.

downgraded_or_rejected.title: statusline-mux raw interpolation
downgraded_or_rejected.reason: Real unquoted interpolation, but every input source (settings.json statusLine.command, the .statusline-original marker) is same-uid/operator-controlled, and an attacker who can write either already has same-uid write to the exec'd mux script and settings.json directly. No privilege boundary is crossed — a quoting defect, not an exploitable injection. Worth fixing for hygiene; not a vuln.

downgraded_or_rejected.title: Tailer offset not reset on in-place truncation
downgraded_or_rejected.reason: Real correctness/availability degradation (silent stall, mid-record resume) requiring a same-uid writer; yields only UI staleness / garbage partials, no corruption or cross-boundary primitive. Folded into T-9 as a robustness fix.

downgraded_or_rejected.title: Bridge stdin single availableData read
downgraded_or_rejected.reason: The scanner itself concluded this path is SAFE — single read = no unbounded accumulation, the exit-0 invariant holds, malformed/oversized input fails to CC's native prompt (safe default). A negative coverage note, not a finding. Dropped from the vuln list.

fix_themes.theme: Lock down ~/.zackeyes (0700 dirs, 0600 marker/files) + verify bundle signature before exec
In-app integrity verification of the update artifact (signature/checksum) + reconstruct URL + reject foreign redirect hosts
Centralize untrusted-text sanitization at one boundary (strip C0/C1/DEL + bidi) for every sink
Size-cap + symlink-skip every untrusted read; clamp integer accumulation; cap the tailer buffer; finite socket timeout
Move the socket to a per-user 0700 dir + client-side peer auth
